findings.evidence: `Positivity.lean:36-38`: "Conservation of angular momentum along the collision axis allows exactly one independent off-diagonal entry in this basis, the double-helicity-flip amplitude connecting `(+1/2, +1/2)` with `(-1/2, -1/2)`". The witness at `ComplexSpinDensity.lean:351-356` is separated from time reversal by `ρ idxPP idxPM = -i`, one of the entries that sentence says vanishes.
findings.fix: Drop the theorem and the corresponding docstring claims, or restrict the statement to the helicity-conserving entries and say explicitly that the separation needs entries forbidden in the forward direction. If the separation is kept, do not advertise it as a statement about forward helicity amplitudes.
findings.issue: `exists_isParityInvariant_not_isTimeReversalInvariant` ("**Parity does not imply time reversal.**", also claimed in the module docstring, lines 22-25) is true only because `SpinDensityC` imposes no angular-momentum conservation. Its witness `v = (1, i, i, 1)` is non-real exactly at the entries `(idxPP, idxPM)` etc., which are zero in a forward helicity-amplitude matrix. On the physically allowed support (diagonal plus the `(idxPP, idxMM)` pair) `IsParityInvariant` as defined gives `mat idxMM idxPP = mat idxPP idxMM`, hermiticity gives `mat idxMM idxPP = conj (mat idxPP idxMM)`, so every entry is real and `IsTimeReversalInvariant` holds: parity does imply time reversal there. The stated theorem therefore presents as physics a conclusion that only its unphysical sector supports.

findings.evidence: The only consumers in this PR (`mat_idxMM_idxMM`, `mat_idxMP_idxMP`, `im_transversity`, lines 177-204) use `h` at `(idxPP, idxPP)`, `(idxPM, idxPM)` and `(idxMM, idxPP)` — all pairs where the phase is `+1`. Only line 348's witness uses the rest.
findings.fix: Either restrict the predicate to the helicity-conserving entries (where the relation is unambiguous and `f1_eq_of_parityInvariant`, `deltaQ_eq_of_parityInvariant`, `IsParityInvariant.im_transversity` all still follow), or carry the phase explicitly; and in either case stop claiming the off-diagonal strengthening as additional physical content.
findings.issue: `IsParityInvariant` is stated phase-free for all index pairs (`∀ i j, mat i.rev j.rev = mat i j`), and the docstring (lines 165-172) sells this as strictly more faithful than the real predicate ("this constrains the off-diagonal entries too"). The Jacob-Wick parity relation for 2→2 helicity amplitudes carries `(-1)^{(Λ-λ)-(Λ'-λ')}`, which is `+1` exactly on the entries with `Λ-λ = Λ'-λ'` — i.e. on the diagonal and the `(idxPP, idxMM)` pair, and `-1` on the other off-diagonals. So the extra off-diagonal content the docstring advertises is sign-convention-dependent, and it is precisely the content the theorem at line 348 relies on.

findings.evidence: Lines 137-144: docstrings versus the stated RHS `(ρ.mat idxPP idxPP).re + (ρ.mat idxMM idxMM).re`; equality of the two entries is exactly `IsParityInvariant.mat_idxMM_idxMM` (line 177), which is not a hypothesis here.
findings.fix: Say "the sum of the two aligned (resp. anti-aligned) diagonal entries", or add "which parity invariance makes twice a single entry".
findings.issue: `f1_add_deltaQ`'s docstring says "`f₁ + Δq` is twice the aligned diagonal entry", but the statement is `(mat idxPP idxPP).re + (mat idxMM idxMM).re`, the sum of two distinct entries; they coincide only under parity. Same at line 143 for `f1_sub_deltaQ` ("twice the anti-aligned diagonal entry"). This undercuts the module's own emphasis that `soffer_bound` uses no parity.

summary: The complex matrix, the Soffer bound, the RCLike entrywise bound and the real/complex equivalence are faithful. The parity material is not: `exists_isParityInvariant_not_isTimeReversalInvariant` asserts a physical separation that does not exist for forward helicity amplitudes, and survives only on entries that forward angular-momentum conservation forbids.
